purpose: The features a plan, product or upgrade includes, each behind a check mark, in one or two columns. It is the "what you get" list of a plan card, an upgrade card or a change-plan drawer: short labels, an optional one-line description under each, and a check that says "included", never "done". It replaces the hand-written `ul` with a `pi pi-check` per row that the billing pages and the change-plan drawer drew with different icon colours.
useWhen: The perks of an upgrade card (Upgrade to Pro: Unlimited Applications, Unlimited Workloads, Custom Domains).
The features a plan includes in a change-plan or upgrade drawer, each with a short description.
Any short list of included capabilities where the check is the only marker.
avoidWhen: Steps or tasks with a done/not-done state (a production checklist, a setup guide) → use `outcome-mark` per row, or the `stepper`.
A comparison of features across plans → use `compare-plans` or `table`.
Rows that navigate or carry actions → use `item`.
Marketing pricing cards on the site → use `card-pricing` / `pricing-plans`, which carry their own feature lists.
related: key-value-pairs` — the plan facts that sit next to the feature list in a billing card.
card` — the surface the list sits in; FeatureList brings no surface of its own.
outcome-mark` — the mark for a step that finished, which this check is not.
bestPractices: Keep each label to a few words in title case or sentence case, one capability per row; put the detail in `description`, not in the label.
Use `columns: 2` for six or more short labels in a wide card; it falls back to one column in a narrow box on its own.
Name the list with `ariaLabel` (for example "Pro plan features") when no visible heading right above it says what the features belong to.
Do not hand-write the list with your own check icons: the check colour and spacing are part of the component.
